source.title: Solution to some open problems on E-super vertex magic labeling of disconnected graphs

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite simple undirected graph with vertex set V(G), edge set E(G), p = |V(G)|, q = |E(G)|, and neighbor set N(u). An E-super vertex magic labeling of G is a bijection f from V(G) union E(G) to {1, 2, 3, ..., p+q} such that f(E(G)) = {1, 2, 3, ..., q} and there is a constant k with f(u) + sum_{v in N(u)} f(uv) = k for every vertex u. With C_n denoting the n-cycle and mC_n denoting m disjoint copies of C_n, can one prove that no graph in either family (2t - 1)C_3 union C_4 or (2t)C_3 union C_5 admits an E-super vertex magic labeling?
accepted.context_brief: E-super vertex magic labelings of disconnected cycle unions

evidence.page: ScienceDirect article page, section 'Solution of some open problems on E-super vertex magic labeling of disconnected graphs'
evidence.quote: Can it be proven that graphs of the form (2t − 1)C_{3}UC_{4} or (2t)C_{3}UC_{5} never possess an E-super vertex magic labeling?
